price_note: DOW.NZ is a thin, effectively untradeable secondary NZX listing of ASX-primary Downer EDI (ASX: DOW). The Yahoo Finance DOW.NZ quote (NZ$0.00063) is a stale data artefact frozen at 20-Jul-2024 with null bars since -- it must NOT be used. current_price is set to the live ASX: DOW price of A$7.80 (verified 2026-08-10 via Yahoo DOW.AX chart API). AUDNZD = 1.1993 for reference only; every valuation figure in this file is in AUD and is NOT converted to NZD. Any NZ investor holding the NZX line is economically exposed to the ASX-line, AUD-denominated risk with none of the liquidity benefit of a real market -- a structural, non-fundamental risk specific to the NZX ticker.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: H1-2026 (31-Dec-2025) WANOS, already reflecting on-market buyback execution. FY2025 year-end count was 671.6m.
inputs.net_debt_basis: H1-2026 (31-Dec-2025) balance sheet. Per company convention, 'net debt' excludes IFRS-16 lease liabilities (borrowings less cash); lease liabilities are instead treated as a cash operating cost via the lease-principal deduction in owner FCF, consistent with 2CC.NZ/TAH.NZ treatment in this repo.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2025 cash flow statement 'Share-based payments expense' add-back; immaterial (~0.04% of revenue), not a material valuation driver for this ticker

buyback_program.note: A$230m on-market buyback approved 21-Aug-2025 (after FY2025 year-end), ~5% of issued capital. H1-2026 cash flow statement shows A$64.4m actually spent (8.3m shares at ~A$7.76 avg). Remaining A$165.6m modelled as retiring a further ~21.2m shares at A$7.80 in Year 1 of the projection, consistent with 'approximately 12.5m shares repurchased by mid-2026' cumulative guidance and the program's pace.

inputs.annual_share_growth_note: After the current buyback program completes (~Year 1), a modest ongoing net reduction of ~0.3%/yr is modelled (continued smaller buybacks roughly offsetting normal LTI-related dilution), consistent with management's stated capital-return posture and improved balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.8x).
inputs.lease_accounting_note: IFRS-16 lease liabilities are material for this plant/fleet-heavy contractor (FY2025 lease principal repayment A$147.6m vs A$439.6m reported FCF -- a 34% deduction). D&A add-back in the component build includes IFRS-16 right-of-use depreciation (A$140.9m of the A$342.5m FY2025 total D&A) as a genuinely non-cash item; the SEPARATE cash lease-principal repayment (a financing-activity cash outflow) is deducted once in owner FCF. These are distinct accounting items (ROU depreciation vs principal repayment) so there is no double-count.

historical_growth.eps_cagr_note: EPS CAGR is not meaningful: FY2020 (COVID, -26.6c) and FY2023 (accounting scandal, -59.0c) are both negative, breaking the CAGR formula at every plausible start year. TTM EPS (to Dec-2025) is ~24.1c on 668.2m shares.
historical_growth.fcf_3yr_cagr_note: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (FY2022 45.6 -> FY2025 271.4) is inflated by starting from a near-trough year and is NOT used as the growth driver -- shown for completeness only.
historical_growth.fcf_5yr_cagr_note: Owner FCF was negative in FY2020 (-331.3) and FY2023 (-121.1), breaking the standard CAGR formula over any 5yr window including those years. A cleaner 4yr span avoiding both negative years (FY2021 232.7 -> FY2025 271.4) gives +3.92%/yr.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue is DECLINING (-1.5%/yr 3yr, -3.7%/yr 5yr) by explicit management design (portfolio simplification: divested Cleaning/Catering/Laundries and the Keolis Downer JV stake to shed low-margin, high-risk revenue). Equity CAGR is also negative (-7.3%/3yr, -3.1%/5yr), driven by the FY2020 COVID loss, the FY2023 accounting-scandal writedown (NPAT -385.7m), and ongoing capital returns (dividends + buyback) reducing retained equity. Owner FCF CAGR is not usable due to two negative years in the window. None of the standard CAGR anchors are reliable growth proxies for this business in transition -- the DCF instead builds revenue and margin paths directly from FY2026 guidance (NPATA A$295-315m, EBITA margin improving from 4.4% FY25 toward a stated 5%+ floor) and management's explicit 'revenue slightly lower than FY25' guidance, rather than extrapolating any single historical CAGR forward.
historical_growth.notes: Do not use reported FCF CAGR either: reported FCF swung from -A$173.6m (FY2020) to +A$430.1m (FY2021) to +A$55.2m (FY2023) to +A$439.6m (FY2025) -- an 8-year EBITDA range of A$82.7m to A$829.2m (>10x peak-to-trough) confirms this is a genuinely high-cyclicality name where no single historical growth rate should be trusted; the WACC premium (see wacc_rationale) is the primary mechanism used to price this risk instead.

bull.narrative: Defence PAS ramps strongly ($3.05bn contract), energy-transition transmission/substation work and Facilities growth (Stockland A$500m) offset Transport declines; class action mediation and ACCC proceedings resolve without material cash cost; EBITA margin exceeds the stated 5%+ floor durably (mature EBITDA margin 8.2%); buyback continues, shares shrink further.

bear.narrative: Class action mediation (Dec-2025) and/or ACCC price-fixing proceedings crystallize a material cash settlement/penalty; margin turnaround stalls or reverses (a repeat of the FY2023 contract-mispricing pattern given the structurally thin ~5% EBITA base); NZ Transport/CRL and Auckland Airport work rolls off with no replacement; AU state Transport-agency budgets stay soft; revenue keeps declining without margin offsetting it.

wacc_rationale.base_cost_of_equity_build: AU 10yr risk-free ~4.3% + equity risk premium ~5.5% x beta ~1.0 (diversified infra-services contractor) = ~9.8%
wacc_rationale.base_wacc_unadjusted_build: Blend of ~9.8% cost of equity (~80% weight) and ~3.85% after-tax cost of debt (BBB-rated, ~5.5% pre-tax x (1-30% tax), ~20% weight given net debt/EBITDA 0.8-0.9x) = ~9.0%

premiums.name: extreme cyclicality / thin margin
premiums.rationale: 8-year EBITDA has ranged A$82.7m (FY2023) to A$829.2m (FY2021) -- a >10x peak-to-trough range, far beyond the 3x threshold that per policy warrants +1.0-2.0%. At a ~4-5% underlying EBITA margin, a handful of mispriced contracts (as happened in FY2023) can erase most of group profit.

premiums.name: unresolved binary legal overhangs
premiums.rationale: (a) Consolidated Victorian Supreme Court shareholder class action over FY20-23 Utilities revenue/WIP misreporting -- court-ordered mediation held by 12-Dec-2025, outcome/quantum not publicly confirmed; (b) ACCC civil proceedings (commenced Dec-2024) against subsidiary Spotless alongside Ventia and BGIS alleging Defence estate-maintenance price-fixing 2019-2022, denied but unresolved. Both are live contingent liabilities generating ongoing legal costs (A$6.3m pre-tax in 1H26 alone) with unquantified tail risk to cash and reputation.

premiums.name: government-contract concentration
premiums.rationale: ~90% of work-in-hand ($38.2bn) is government/quasi-government-related, exposing the business to public infrastructure budget cycles and election-driven spending decisions, as already evidenced by soft AU state Transport-agency spend.

wacc_rationale.small_cap_illiquidity_note: No small-cap illiquidity premium applied -- ASX: DOW has a ~A$5.1bn market cap and normal ASX liquidity. The NZX secondary line (DOW.NZ) IS illiquid to the point of showing zero trades and a stale quote, but that is a listing-venue artefact, not a fundamental risk to the underlying business, and is disclosed qualitatively in price_note rather than priced into WACC.
wacc_rationale.terminal_growth_rationale: Modest, below-nominal-GDP terminal growth appropriate for a mature, low-single-digit-margin government contractor with no structural growth premium once the current margin-recovery/portfolio-simplification cycle completes.

valuation.horizon_note: 10-year explicit build used because this is a cyclical, margin-recovering business emerging from a scandal-depressed trough; the extended horizon lets the margin-recovery and normalization (capex, tax rate) play out fully before terminal capitalization, rather than capitalizing an immature or still-transitioning margin at Year 5.

base.implied_exit_multiple_note: 10.49x terminal-year owner FCF, equivalent under the Gordon formula to (1+2.25%)/(12.0%-2.25%). Cross-checked against the historical 6.12-9.06x EV/EBITDA range (ex-FY2020/FY2023 outliers) -- the bound was Gordon, not the caps, and sits moderately above the top of the historical EV/EBITDA band on an EV/FCF-equivalent basis, reflecting owner FCF being a smaller multiple base than EBITDA once lease principal, capex and cash tax are all deducted.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (10%-14%), columns = terminal growth (1.25%-3.25%). Top-left row flattens at 4.20 because the 13x terminal-FCF multiple cap binds at low WACC / high terminal growth combinations, preventing the Gordon formula from blowing up as (WACC - g) narrows.

price_range_10yr.position: upper portion of 10yr range -- current price is within ~10% of the 10yr high, consistent with the market pricing in a durable margin turnaround

sanity_check.diagnosis: The DCF is not overstating value (the usual failure mode this gate exists to catch) -- it is understating relative to trading multiples, i.e. the trip fired on the LOW side. Investigated three candidate causes: (1) double-counting lease costs (D&A add-back + lease-principal deduction) -- ruled out: FY2025 D&A of A$342.5m includes only A$140.9m of IFRS-16 right-of-use depreciation (a genuinely non-cash item), while the A$147.6m lease-PRINCIPAL repayment is a separate cash financing outflow; these are distinct line items with no overlap. (2) WACC stack too punitive -- the 12.0% base WACC (9.0% unadjusted + 1.5% cyclicality + 1.0% legal + 0.5% govt-concentration) is high but each premium is independently justified by disclosed, quantified risks (>10x EBITDA peak-to-trough range; two live unresolved legal/regulatory proceedings; ~90% government revenue concentration) rather than an arbitrary stack. (3) Owner-FCF base too conservative -- this is the primary driver: after deducting IFRS-16 lease principal (A$147.6m, 34% of reported FCF), even FY2025's PEAK owner FCF of A$271.4m implies an owner-FCF yield on enterprise value of only ~4.8-5.3%, well below the 12% WACC, and the approximate perpetuity-equivalent owner FCF needed to justify the current A$7.80 price at a 12% WACC / 2.25% terminal growth is ~A$552m -- roughly DOUBLE the FY2025 peak. This is a genuine, structural finding about this business (thin owner-FCF conversion once real lease/capex/tax costs are all charged) rather than a modeling artefact.
sanity_check.fix_applied: No mechanical 'fix' was applied because the trip is not evidence of an error -- it is evidence that the market (at A$7.80, upper-decile of the 10yr price range, 9.0x TTM EV/EBITDA) is pricing a stronger and more durable margin-recovery/multiple-re-rating story than a conservative, lease-cost-inclusive owner-FCF DCF supports. What WAS done in response to the trip: (a) the terminal value is capped at min(Gordon, 13x terminal FCF, 7.49x terminal EBITDA) so a single aggressive assumption cannot silently re-inflate the terminal value past what the market has historically paid; (b) the bull case (WACC 11%, mature EBITDA margin 8.2%, still using historical multiple caps) is provided as the counter-scenario reflecting the turnaround thesis, and even bull case shows -26.3% downside, which is disclosed prominently rather than suppressed; (c) both the DCF-implied multiples and the historical trading-multiple table are published side by side in this JSON so a reader can independently judge whether they trust the cash-flow-based view or the multiple-based (market) view more.
sanity_check.verification_note: This is a case where the sanity check correctly flags a wide gap between DCF and market pricing rather than a bug to be silently reconciled. The gap is disclosed, quantified and explained rather than papered over with an unjustified WACC reduction or margin assumption.

valuation_philosophy: Downer EDI is a structurally thin-margin (historically ~5-6% EBITDA margin), plant- and fleet-heavy government-services contractor that is only ~2-3 years removed from a major accounting-irregularities scandal (FY2023 NPAT -A$385.7m) and still carries two significant unresolved legal/regulatory overhangs (a shareholder class action in mediation and ACCC price-fixing proceedings against its Spotless subsidiary). Because roughly A$140-165m/year of IFRS-16 lease principal is a genuine, recurring cash cost of running its plant and vehicle fleet -- not financing flexibility -- this model deducts it in full from reported free cash flow to arrive at 'owner FCF', consistent with how other lease-heavy, plant-intensive names in this research library (2CC.NZ, TAH.NZ) are treated. On that conservative but realistic basis, even FY2025's cyclical PEAK owner FCF (A$271.4m, after also stripping A$16.9m of interest income and A$3.7m of stock-based compensation) supports a base-case intrinsic value of only A$3.18/share -- 59% below the current A$7.80 ASX price -- once discounted at a WACC (12.0%) that is explicitly loaded for the business's demonstrated cyclicality (an 8-year EBITDA range of A$82.7m to A$829.2m, a >10x peak-to-trough swing), its two live binary legal risks, and its ~90% government-revenue concentration. The probability-weighted intrinsic value across bull/base/bear scenarios is A$3.32, and even the bull case (a durable margin turnaround to an 8.2% mature EBITDA margin at a lower 11% WACC) values the stock at A$5.75, still 26% below the current price. This does not mean the market is 'wrong' -- it means the market at A$7.80 (near the top of its 10-year A$2.93-A$8.59 range, at 9.0x TTM EV/EBITDA versus a 6.1-9.1x historical band) is pricing a stronger, more durable version of the ongoing margin-recovery and portfolio-simplification story than a conservative cash-flow build supports, and/or is pricing owner FCF net of lease costs more generously than this model does. Readers who believe management's FY2026 guidance (underlying NPATA A$295-315m) will translate into a durable EBITDA margin materially above 7% AND that both legal overgangs resolve immaterially should weight the bull case more heavily; readers who recall that the FY2023 scandal also began as 'a few mispriced contracts' in a similarly thin-margin business should weight the bear case (A$1.18/share) more heavily. The entry price of A$2.52 (the price that would deliver a 15% IRR including the full 10-year interim owner-FCF path and net debt) is provided as the buy-discipline anchor rather than the terminal-value-only shortcut.
